notes.summary: Partial P15.1 theorem: for a supplied holomorphic fibration and pullback Kähler class, bounded unnormalized relative base energy is independent of calibrated Kähler directions, including non-descending bounded approximants with uniform convergence and no epsilon-relative rate. Singular fibres are included; the original general atom remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: Let pi:X->B be surjective between connected smooth compact Kähler manifolds, n>nu>=1, theta=pi*beta, m=n-nu, K=binom(n,nu), and V=int_B beta^nu. The degree-zero current pi_*(omega^m) is a positive constant c. For bounded beta-psh phi and any bounded (theta+epsilon omega_epsilon)-psh u_epsilon uniformly converging to pi*phi, with omega_epsilon smoothly converging to any Kähler form, the calibrated energy converges to the raw E_beta(phi), with error O(delta_epsilon)+O(epsilon), without delta_epsilon=o(epsilon). Relative cocycles, shifts by bV, monotonicity, concavity, bounded affine variations, continuous C1 uniform-path first variations, and compensating base-reference changes are proved. Exact bounded-current projection holds through critical values. No unbounded P-type, E1 completion, canonical carrier, arbitrary degenerate path, or solution for a general pseudoeffective zero-volume class is claimed. This is an unverified author draft with explicit standard foundations.
notes.text:
This is partial progress on P15.1, not a complete solution of the original general pseudoeffective zero-volume problem. The authoritative full proof is P15.1-argument.md; the standalone full-proof paper is P15.1-partial.tex and its twice-compiled P15.1-partial.pdf. The operator proposal and earlier comparison-paper verdicts are not proof premises. No companion-task output was used.

Exact setting and claim. Use ddc=i/(2pi) partial barpartial and dc=i/(4pi)(barpartial-partial). Let pi:X->B be a supplied surjective holomorphic map between connected smooth compact Kähler manifolds of dimensions n and nu, 1<=nu<n, with m=n-nu. Neither smooth fibres, flatness, equidimensionality, nor a product is assumed. Fix a Kähler form beta on B, theta=pi*beta, V=int_B beta^nu, K=binom(n,nu). For bounded beta-psh phi let U=phi composed with pi and C_phi=beta+ddc phi. Bounded means everywhere finite bounded quasi-psh representatives; convergence uses the pointwise uniform norm.

For any Kähler omega, pi_*(omega^m)=c_omega is a positive constant. More generally take Kähler omega_epsilon converging smoothly to any Kähler omega_0, and write c_epsilon=pi_*(omega_epsilon^m), q_epsilon=theta+epsilon omega_epsilon, s_epsilon=K c_epsilon epsilon^m. For any bounded q_epsilon-psh u_epsilon with delta_epsilon=||u_epsilon-U||_infinity->0, the unnormalized energy E_q(v)=(1/(d+1)) sum_(j=0)^d int_Y v(q+ddc v)^j q^(d-j) satisfies E_q_epsilon(u_epsilon)/s_epsilon -> E_beta(phi). No descent of u_epsilon or epsilon-relative rate is assumed. If bounded v_epsilon uniformly approximates pi*psi under the same backgrounds, the calibrated relative energies converge to R_beta(phi,psi), where R_q(v,w)=(1/(d+1)) sum_j int_Y(v-w)T_v^j T_w^(d-j). One may replace c_epsilon by c_omega_0. A supporting estimate proves pi_*((q_epsilon+ddc u_epsilon)^n)/s_epsilon -> C_phi^nu weakly on B, with raw mass V. This does not claim to solve general P15.2.

Imported foundations. Locally bounded psh potentials define closed positive symmetric Bedford–Taylor products recursively by ddc(p S); simultaneous local decreasing smooth psh regularizations yield weak convergence of mixed products. Citation: Bedford and Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math.149 (1982),1–40, Section2; Fine topology, Shilov boundary, and (ddc)^n, J. Funct. Anal.72 (1987),225–251. The bounded construction is also stated in BEGZ arXiv:0812.3674v2 LF175–188, with a local continuity application at LF668–679. Multilinearity here follows by smooth local approximation and finite expansion. The bounded special case of BEGZ Theorem1.14/Lemma1.15 states: on a compact Kähler manifold, for closed positive bidimension(1,1) Theta and bounded quasi-psh differences a,b, int a ddc b Theta = int b ddc a Theta = -int db dc a Theta; these integrals are finite and da dc a Theta is a finite positive measure. Citation: Boucksom, Eyssidieux, Guedj, Zeriahi, Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, Acta Math.205 (2010),199–262; primary LF626–762. Every application uses A=empty, globally bounded quasi-psh differences, and closed positive mixed BT currents of the required bidimension. The standard nef convention identifies positive products with cup products, volume with the top product, and nef numerical dimension with max{k:int alpha^k kappa^(n-k)>0}; BEGZ Definition1.17 and discussion, LF810–840. These apply because theta is smooth semipositive. Stokes for currents and Sard's smooth critical-value theorem are used; Sard, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.48 (1942),883–890.

Transverse constant and numerical data. Proper holomorphic pushforward of the closed positive (m,m) form omega^m is closed positive of degree zero. A scalar distribution with zero derivatives is constant: local convolution gives functions with zero gradient, and overlaps and connectedness give one constant. Thus pi_*omega^m=c on all B, without a critical-value-supported term. Surjectivity and Sard give a full-rank open set. Consequently int_X theta^nu omega^m>0, and c=(int_X theta^nu omega^m)/V>0. At any regular value, ordinary submersion-coordinate fibre integration gives c=int_(pi^-1(b)) omega^m, summed over disconnected components. Stokes gives representative independence in a fixed auxiliary class; c_(t omega)=t^m c_omega, so c is not class independent. Since theta^(nu+1)=0 and the nu-th mixed intersection is positive, alpha=[theta] is nef, pseudoeffective, volume zero, and numerical dimension nu. Its perturbative volume is sum_(k=0)^nu binom(n,k)epsilon^(n-k) int_X theta^k omega^(n-k), hence K c V epsilon^m+O(epsilon^(m+1)). Smooth auxiliary convergence bounds these coefficients and gives c_epsilon->c_omega_0>0.

Bounded projection through singular fibres. On base charts write each positive bounded-potential factor C_i=ddc p_i with p_i locally bounded psh. The compositions p_i composed with pi are locally bounded psh; their BT products define the pullback products. Local smooth decreasing approximations on the base pull back and converge in BT sense. Products of more than nu base factors vanish at the smooth levels by dimension, hence at the limit on all X. For k<=nu, set P_0=omega^m and P_r=ddc((p_r composed with pi)P_(r-1)). Bounded Borel multiplication of order-zero currents gives pi_*((g composed with pi)S)=g pi_*S by integration of coefficient measures against pulled-back test forms. Proper holomorphic pushforward commutes with ddc. Induction gives pi_*P_r=ddc(p_r pi_*P_(r-1))=c C_r...C_1. Thus pi_*(pi*C_1...pi*C_k omega^m)=c C_1...C_k on every chart, including critical values. This asserts no projection theorem for arbitrary singular currents. For a+b=nu and bounded Borel g, it gives int_X(g composed with pi)H^a theta^b omega^m=c int_B g C_phi^a beta^b, where H=theta+ddc U. Taking g=phi justifies the discontinuously weighted energy term exactly, without testing a weak limit against phi.

Mixed masses. Replacing one bounded-potential current q_i+ddc w_i by q_i changes a mixed product by the globally exact current ddc(w_i S), where S is the remaining closed product. Boundedness makes w_i S order zero; local BT recursion verifies the identity and patches globally. Stokes gives the ordinary cup-product mixed masses, including semipositive theta and the mixed currents below.

Bounded energy laws. For a Kähler background q on a compact d-fold, all mixed masses equal V_q=int q^d, so E_q(0)=0 and E_q(v+b)=E_q(v)+b V_q. Along v_t=(1-t)w+tv with bounded q-psh endpoints and h=v-w, the energy is a finite polynomial. Differentiate and apply bounded IBP with a=v_t, b=h, Theta=T_v_t^(j-1)q^(d-j). The second contribution becomes j int h(T_v_t-q)T_v_t^(j-1)q^(d-j). The sum telescopes to dE_q(v_t)/dt=int h T_v_t^d, with one-sided endpoint derivatives. Integrating and using int_0^1 binom(d,j)t^j(1-t)^(d-j)dt=1/(d+1) gives E_q(v)-E_q(w)=R_q(v,w). Hence R_q(v,w)+R_q(w,z)=R_q(v,z). Ordered endpoints give monotonicity. Comparing v with w plus or minus ||v-w|| gives |E_q(v)-E_q(w)|<=V_q||v-w||. A second differentiation and IBP with a=b=h, Theta=T_v_t^(d-1), gives d²E/dt²=-d int dh dc h T_v_t^(d-1)<=0, proving concavity with the finite positive BT gradient-square measure.

An additional first-variation scope is a C1 path into C(Y) with the uniform norm, every v_t q-psh. For uniform a_l->a, telescoping mixed products and smooth testing with -C_f q<=ddc f<=C_f q gives |int f(T_a_l^j T_a^(d-j)-T_a^d)|<=j C_f V_q||a_l-a||. Equal masses extend convergence to continuous tests. Divide the relative energy formula for v_(t+h),v_t by h: velocities converge uniformly to continuous dot v_t and mixed measures converge weakly, giving dE_q(v_t)/dt=int dot v_t T_v_t^d. No variation for arbitrary discontinuous velocities is inferred; the nonsmooth second variation stated above is for affine segments.

Leading energy and no-rate stability. Expand (H+epsilon omega_epsilon)^j(theta+epsilon omega_epsilon)^(n-j). Only terms with a+b<=nu horizontal factors survive. At power epsilon^m the coefficient of int U H^a theta^(nu-a)omega_epsilon^m is (1/(n+1))sum_j binom(j,a)binom(n-j,nu-a)=K/(nu+1). Count (nu+1)-element subsets of {1,...,n+1} by their (a+1)-st element to prove the identity. Exact weighted projection yields E_q_epsilon(U)=s_epsilon E_beta(phi)+O(||phi||epsilon^(m+1)). Each remaining absolute integral is bounded by ||phi|| int_X theta^(a+b)omega_epsilon^(n-a-b), using positive mixed masses. The energy Lipschitz bound gives |E_q_epsilon(u_epsilon)-E_q_epsilon(U)|<=delta_epsilon int q_epsilon^n. After calibration, the total error is at most delta_epsilon(V+O(epsilon))+O(||phi||epsilon). This proves the energy limit; applying it twice proves the relative limit. A non-descending admissible example with slower convergence is u_epsilon=sqrt(epsilon)pi*f+epsilon zeta at phi=0, where f is smooth nonconstant and zeta is a sufficiently small smooth function varying on a regular fibre with omega+ddc zeta>0. Then beta+sqrt(epsilon)ddc f>0 for small epsilon, and the uniform error has order sqrt(epsilon).

Supporting measure estimate. Set A=q_epsilon+ddc u_epsilon, D=H+epsilon omega_epsilon. Factor A^n-D^n=ddc(u_epsilon-U)sum_(j=0)^(n-1)A^jD^(n-1-j). For smooth real f on B, bound plus/minus pi*ddc f by C_f theta. Bounded IBP gives |int (f composed with pi)(A^n-D^n)|<=n C_f delta_epsilon I_epsilon, where every mixed theta integral equals I_epsilon=int theta q_epsilon^(n-1). Its leading term is binom(n-1,nu-1)c_epsilon V epsilon^m; therefore I_epsilon/s_epsilon=(nu/n)V+O(epsilon), and the scaled difference is O_f(delta_epsilon). The exact pullback expansion is pi_*D^n=s_epsilon C_phi^nu+sum_(k=0)^(nu-1)binom(n,k)epsilon^(n-k)pi_*(H^k omega_epsilon^(n-k)). Its positive remainder has calibrated total variation O(epsilon). Scaled A measures have masses V+O(epsilon), so smooth approximation proves weak convergence on continuous tests. Total-variation convergence for arbitrary A is not asserted.

References and path scopes. Arbitrary auxiliary Kähler classes yield the identical base limit using their respective c. Smoothly convergent Kähler families have uniformly bounded coefficients and c bounded away from zero; instantaneous and limiting-c calibrations agree. No arbitrary degenerate auxiliary path is claimed. For beta'=beta+ddc h Kähler, compensate phi'=phi-h and psi'=psi-h. Represented currents and potential differences are unchanged, giving R_beta'(phi-h,psi-h)=R_beta(phi,psi). Since h is beta-psh, E_beta'(phi-h)=E_beta(phi)-E_beta(h); V is unchanged. At positive epsilon, H_h=pi*h, q'_epsilon=q_epsilon+ddc H_h, u'_epsilon=u_epsilon-H_h give exactly E_q'_epsilon(u'_epsilon)=E_q_epsilon(u_epsilon)-E_q_epsilon(H_h). Thus reference correction survives the limit. The compact Kähler ddc lemma supplies h for cohomologous smooth representatives: an exact real smooth closed (1,1) form is ddc of a smooth real function; Deligne, Griffiths, Morgan, Sullivan, Invent. Math.29 (1975),245–274. The formulas themselves assume the exhibited h.

Optional continuous descent. With connected fibres, continuous theta-psh W descends uniquely to continuous beta-psh phi. The additional standard foundation is analytic resolution of each compact irreducible reduced complex analytic space by a smooth connected compact complex manifold; Bierstone and Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero by blowing up the maximum strata of a local invariant, Invent. Math.128 (1997),207–302, Main Theorem in the complex analytic category. Resolve each reduced irreducible fibre component. W pulls back to a psh function, since a local base potential is constant there. The compact smooth psh maximum principle makes it constant. Constants agree on intersecting components, and connectedness makes W constant on the entire fibre. The proper surjection is a quotient map, hence phi is continuous. Finally pi_*((theta+ddc W)omega^m)=c(beta+ddc phi) is positive. Local convolution and limiting submean inequalities show phi is beta-psh through critical values. Resolution is not needed for the main supplied-pullback theorem.

Limitations. The carrier is the supplied B, with reference beta, potential zero, and raw mass V>0. Constants shift energy by bV. All treated potentials have bounded/minimal singularity type. The positive transverse calibration is not division by vol(alpha)=0; the full leading volume coefficient is K c V, and dividing by it would normalize away V. No reconstruction from I-equivalence is asserted. The result extends the old smooth fixed-class calculation, but requires the supplied fibration and pullback Kähler hypothesis. No canonical carrier, globally minimal reference scale, independence under changing pi, E1 completion, prescribed unbounded P-type, or arbitrary degenerate-direction theorem is proved. Original P15.1 remains open. This is an unverified author proof, not an independent mathematical verdict.
